samples.summary: New docs `setImageUrlResolver` seam has no test at all, unlike every sibling engine
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts` adds `setImageUrlResolver` and applies it in `getOrLoadImage` (line 57). There is no test file for it: `packages/docs/src/view/` contains only `image-cache.ts` and `image-selection-overlay.ts` (glob `packages/docs/src/view/*image*`), and grepping `setImageUrlResolver` across the repo shows dedicated tests for the identical seam in slides (`packages/slides/test/view/canvas/image-cache-resolver.test.ts`), notes (`packages/notes/src/view/preview-image-resolver.test.ts`) and sheets (`packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-cache.test.ts`) but nothing for docs. So the four behaviors those tests pin — fetching the resolved URL rather than the logical src, identity-by-default, `null` restoring identity, cache keyed by the resolved URL — are unverified for docs. If the seam is mis-wired, every share-link-uploaded image 403s and never renders (the exact failure mode the diff claims to fix).

samples.summary: The new unauthenticated upload route's Multer `fileFilter` (MIME allowlist) and `fileSize` limit are never exercised by its spec
samples.evidence: `image-share-upload.controller.spec.ts` constructs the controller directly (`new ApiV1ShareImageUploadController(...)`) and calls `ctrl.upload(pngFile(), 'tok')`, so the `@UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor(...))` config — `limits.fileSize: IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES` and the `ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` `fileFilter` with `unsupportedFileTypeMessage` — is inert metadata during the test. `pngFile()`'s `mimetype: 'image/png'` is decorative: an `image/svg+xml` or over-cap body would take the exact same code path in this spec. The sibling upload route pins both through supertest (`images.controller.spec.ts:65-105`: 413 on `cap + 1024`, 400 with `Unsupported file type: image/svg+xml`). Since this is the only *unauthenticated* write in the image module, a wrong constant or an omitted filter would ship undetected as arbitrary-type / unbounded-size anonymous upload.

samples.summary: The `["doc", setDocsImageUrlResolver]` installer entry (and its unmount cleanup) has no test
samples.evidence: The only test touching `shared-document.tsx` is `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-blob-routing.test.ts`, which imports `sharedBlobKind` only. Nothing asserts that mounting a shared `doc` installs the docs resolver with the visitor's token or clears it on unmount — the effect-ordering argument added to the comment block (docs canvas created in a child's passive effect) is entirely unverified, and if the resolver is installed too late the first image load fires un-tokened and 403s.

samples.summary: `failureText`'s non-JSON fallback and the `credentials: "include"` on the unauthenticated path are untested
samples.evidence: `image-insert.test.ts` covers only the JSON-with-`message` branch ("surfaces the server's message, not the raw JSON body"). Nothing covers a plain-text/HTML error body (proxy 502), a JSON body without `message`, or the documented `credentials: "include"` on the anonymous `fetch` — the test only inspects `init?.method` (`expect(init?.method).toBe("POST")`). There is no `packages/frontend/src/api/images.test.ts` (glob over `src/api/*` shows only `share-image-url.test.ts`).

samples.summary: The `uploadImageRef` freshness behavior in docs-view is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds a ref + effect so `onImageFileDrop` uses the latest uploader without re-mounting the editor, and passes `uploadImageRef.current` at line 492. No test exercises a drop after the `uploadImage` prop changes (no `docs-view` test file; the only new frontend test is `image-insert.test.ts`, which calls `insertImageFromFile` directly). A stale-ref regression would silently send a share-link visitor's drop through the authenticated uploader — the 401→/login eject this change exists to prevent.

samples.summary: "uses the passed uploader rather than the owner default" is near-vacuous / duplicative
samples.evidence: The test asserts only `upload` was called once and `fetchWithAuth` was not — both already implied by the preceding test in the same describe, which additionally asserts the inserted URL and dimensions. It cannot fail for any behavior the earlier test would not already catch.

samples.summary: `stubImageLoads` mutates `Image.prototype.src` via defineProperty and is never undone
samples.evidence: `Object.defineProperty(Image.prototype, "src", ...)` is not a spy, so `vi.restoreAllMocks()` / `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` do not revert it; the second describe block has no `afterEach` at all. Harmless under vitest's per-file isolation but leaves a global monkey-patch and a module-scope `SRC_SEEN` array that tests must remember to reset by hand.

verdict.reason: The docs `setImageUrlResolver` seam exists and is real (packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:33-44, applied at line 57, exported at src/index.ts:211, consumed by frontend shared-document.tsx:49), but no test anywhere exercises it. Docs tests live in packages/docs/test/ (not src/, where the reviewer looked) and I enumerated all 110 of them: no image-cache/resolver test, and grep for `image-cache` inside packages/docs matches only source importers, so there is no indirect coverage via doc-canvas/paint-layout/table-renderer tests either. I also followed the wiring chain outward: shared-blob-routing.test.ts only tests `sharedBlobKind`; share-image-url.test.ts tests `appendShareTokenToImageUrl` standalone without ever installing it into the docs cache; image-insert.test.ts covers upload/insert and explicitly relies on the untested seam to render later; no e2e image tests exist. The identical seams in slides, notes and sheets each have dedicated tests pinning the four behaviors (resolved-URL fetch, identity default, null restore, cache keyed by resolved URL), so docs is the only unverified one. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed behavior on a user-visible path (share-link viewers loading inline images) with zero meaningful coverage; a mis-wired seam ships as silent 403s/blank images.
groundedIn: packages/docs/test/view/ (110 test files, no image-cache/resolver test)

finding.evidence: `image-share-upload.controller.spec.ts` constructs the controller directly (`new ApiV1ShareImageUploadController(...)`) and calls `ctrl.upload(pngFile(), 'tok')`, so the `@UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor(...))` config — `limits.fileSize: IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES` and the `ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` `fileFilter` with `unsupportedFileTypeMessage` — is inert metadata during the test. `pngFile()`'s `mimetype: 'image/png'` is decorative: an `image/svg+xml` or over-cap body would take the exact same code path in this spec. verdict.reason: The spec for the new unauthenticated upload route instantiates the controller directly (`new ApiV1ShareImageUploadController(...)`) and invokes `ctrl.upload(file, token)` in all seven tests, so the `@UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor(...))` config at image-share-upload.controller.ts:78-92 (fileSize = IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES, fileFilter over ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES) is never executed — deleting either would leave the spec green. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for `ApiV1ShareImageUploadController`, `image-share-upload`, and `shared/images` yields only the controller, its spec, api-v1.module.ts, the frontend client and docs (no supertest/e2e); `packages/backend/test/**` e2e specs contain no `shared` image route; route-collision.spec.ts inspects only PATH/METHOD metadata, not multer options; and image.constants.spec.ts:43-49 is a source-text scan for the message literal that would still pass if this route's filter/limit were removed. The only end-to-end pinning of these two bounds is on the sibling authenticated route (images.controller.spec.ts:65-105). Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a guard on the module's only anonymous write has no meaningful test (missing-test, major impact).
